cards.back: At equilibrium in a simple binding model, the ligand concentration associated with half occupancy.
A change in one binding event's effect on the affinity of additional sites in a multisite system.
Turnover number: catalytic cycles per enzyme molecule per unit time at substrate saturation.
Inhibition that raises apparent Km in the simple model while preserving Vmax at saturating substrate.
An electrochemical proton gradient across a membrane that can power transport and ATP synthesis.
A molecule such as NAD⁺/NADH that transfers electrons between metabolic reactions.
The rate at which material flows through a reaction or pathway.
Use of labeled atoms to follow molecular transformations and estimate pathway flow.
v = Vmax[S]/(Km + [S]); Km is the [S] at half Vmax and is not generally a dissociation constant.
kcat = Vmax/[E]₀ (needs active enzyme); kcat/Km is the low-substrate second-order rate constant.
Competitive: Km×α, Vmax same. Noncompetitive: Vmax/α, Km same. Uncompetitive: both ÷α.
Prefer nonlinear fits over double-reciprocal fits; spread [S] around Km and keep rates initial.
ΔG = ΔG°′ + RT ln Q; direction depends on ΔG, not ΔG°′. RT ≈ 2.58 kJ/mol at 310 K.
Cells hold ATP/ADP far from equilibrium, so cellular ΔG for ATP hydrolysis is more negative than −30.5 kJ/mol.
Standard free energies add when reactions share a mechanism, as in hexokinase's phosphoryl transfer.
ΔG°′ = −nFΔE°′; NADH to O₂ releases about −219 kJ/mol, stored stepwise as a proton gradient.
K_d = [R][L]/[RL]; θ = L_free/(K_d + L_free); half occupied at L_free = K_d.
Use the quadratic when receptor is not ≪ K_d; otherwise binding is overestimated.
Y = Pⁿ/(P₅₀ⁿ + Pⁿ); n > 1 positive cooperativity; n ≤ number of sites.
A sigmoidal curve unloads far more between lung and tissue pressures than a hyperbola.
Base: f(BH⁺) = 1/(1 + 10^(pH − pKa)). Acid: f(A⁻) = 1/(1 + 10^(pKa − pH)). Half at pH = pKa.
pI = average of the two pKa values bracketing the neutral form; neutral amino acids use the α-carboxyl and α-amino pKa values.
Net charge falls as pH rises; above the pI it is negative (moves toward the positive electrode, binds anion exchange).
A group buffers within about one unit of its pKa; histidine (pKa about 6) is the main protein buffer near neutral pH.
K_u = [U]/[N] = exp(−ΔG_unfold/RT); f_N = 1/(1 + K_u); RT = 2.48 kJ/mol at 25 °C.
ΔG_unfold([D]) = ΔG_H₂O − m[D]; midpoint C_m = ΔG_H₂O/m.
ΔΔG of −8 kJ/mol multiplies K_u by about 25; the folded fraction may barely change while the unfolded supply rises sharply.
Stabilities of a few tens of kJ/mol leave a small unfolded population that chaperones and degradation systems must manage.
Glucose → 2 pyruvate with a net 2 ATP and 2 NADH; lactate fermentation reoxidizes the NADH, giving 2 lactate per glucose.
[AMP] ≈ K[ADP]²/[ATP] with K ≈ 1; EC = ([ATP] + ½[ADP])/([ATP] + [ADP] + [AMP]); a 10% fall in ATP can raise AMP several-fold.
Inhibited by ATP and citrate; activated by AMP, ADP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate; sigmoidal in fructose-6-phosphate.
A pool can rise from more production or less consumption; crossover patterns locate a block; flux needs rate measurements.
Δp = Δψ + 61.5 mV × ΔpH at 37 °C; the free energy per mole of protons is F × Δp, about 19 kJ/mol for Δp near 196 mV.
Minimum ≈ ΔG_ATP/(F Δp) ≈ 2.7; measured about 4 including transport; efficiency about 68% in the synthetic example.
4 substrate-level + 10 NADH × 2.5 + 2 FADH₂ × 1.5 = 32 (30 to 32 depending on shuttles); 5.3 ATP per O₂.
Proton return without ATP synthesis lowers ATP per O₂, raises oxygen use and heat, and does not block glycolysis.
J = k₁S in a two-step pathway; A_ss = J/k₂; the same pool can follow more production or less consumption.
C_i = (ΔJ/J)/(ΔE_i/E_i); ΣC_i = 1; a linear prediction holds for small changes only.
Control is shared and condition-dependent; the lowest-activity or most-regulated step need not control flux.
Allosteric: seconds. Covalent: seconds to minutes. Enzyme amount: hours to days (time to 90% = ln 10 × half-life / ln 2).
Average the replicate initial rates at each substrate concentration; report the number of replicates.
1/v = (Km/Vmax)(1/[S]) + 1/Vmax: intercept = 1/Vmax, slope = Km/Vmax; unweighted fits magnify error at low rates.
Vmax unchanged, Km(app) = Km(1 + [I]/K_I); K_I = [I]/(α − 1) with α = Km(app)/Km.
Less than about 10% substrate used, negligible product inhibition, concentrations spread around Km.
No NADH reoxidation at the chain → NADH rises → lactate dehydrogenase makes lactate to regenerate NAD⁺ → lactate is a redox outlet.
Glycolysis to lactate gives 2 ATP per glucose; keeping the same ATP with a blocked chain needs glucose uptake of demand/2 and lactate of two per glucose.
Lactate/pyruvate tracks cytosolic NADH/NAD⁺ at equilibrium; an M+3 lactate fraction divided by the labeled fraction of glucose gives the fraction from medium glucose.
Oxygen consumption, lactate/pyruvate, a glucose tracer and an electron-acceptor rescue; use at least two independent readouts.
